See README.md in this directory for how to run it, how to add a query, and what the acceptance targets are and where they come from. shape is the QueryShape (packages/search/src/query.ts) that packages/search/src/normalise.ts actually assigns to text on classification — every value below was verified against the real normaliseQuery() output, not asserted by hand. category is a coverage label only (exact_error, stack_trace, log, code_fragment, version_rich, natural_language, adversarial, zero_result), matching IMPLEMENTATION.md sec7 and RESEARCH-CONSTRAINTS.md R-22; it is not consumed by evaluate.ts. relevantProblemSlugs are kebab-case slugs invented for this benchmark and matched against the seed corpus once it exists (see README.md for the full list). Queries that share a slug describe the same underlying problem pasted in different shapes, deliberately, to test that retrieval finds it regardless of presentation.

queries.text: postgres.js keeps saying prepared statement already exists after we put pgbouncer in front of it
queries.notes: ADVERSARIAL: a semantic match would likely surface pgbouncer-prepared-statement-does-not-exist-transaction-pooling — near-identical vocabulary (prepared statement, pgbouncer, connection pooling) and even opposite wording (already exists vs does not exist) sit close together in embedding space. The fix here is disabling postgres.js's automatic prepare, not changing PgBouncer's pool_mode; the two playbooks share a cause family but not a remedy.

queries.text: node process crashes with JavaScript heap out of memory even though the container has plenty of RAM to spare
queries.notes: ADVERSARIAL: 'memory' and 'container' co-occurring strongly invite a match on k8s-oomkilled-memory-limit, but the query explicitly states the container has RAM to spare — the cause is V8's own default heap ceiling (--max-old-space-size), unrelated to the pod's resource limit. A semantic-only match that ignores that qualifying clause returns the wrong playbook.

queries.text: wrangler d1 execute says the database is locked when my worker and a cron trigger write at the same time
queries.notes: ADVERSARIAL: 'database locked under concurrent writes' is generic enough to pull in postgres-deadlock-detected-40p01 by pure semantic similarity. D1's single-writer SQLite model needs retry/serialization, not the transaction-ordering fix that resolves a Postgres deadlock — the two are not interchangeable despite the shared vocabulary.

queries.text: cannot find module right after a fresh clone even though npm install finished with no errors
queries.notes: ADVERSARIAL: textually and semantically adjacent to node-err-module-not-found-esm-upgrade (both are Node module-resolution errors), but this one is a missing/mismatched dependency — a lockfile or postinstall problem — not an ESM extension-resolution change. Answering with the ESM playbook sends the reader nowhere.

queries.text: pods stuck ImagePullBackOff in the cluster but docker pull for the same image works fine on my laptop
queries.notes: ADVERSARIAL: heavy lexical overlap ('pull', 'access', 'registry') invites a generic Docker 'pull access denied' / docker-login playbook. The query itself rules that out — docker pull succeeding locally proves registry credentials are fine outside the cluster, so the actual fix is the pod's imagePullSecrets binding, a Kubernetes-side problem, not a Docker-side one.
